The function `_swiglu_fwd` prepares input tensors `x` and `y`, ensuring they are contiguous and splitting them from the input `xy`. It also reshapes the tensors as needed and initializes the output tensor. The grid is defined based on the number of rows (`M`) and columns (`N`) using `triton.cdiv` to calculate blocks per column. The kernel is then launched with the specified grid configuration.
